items.s: With The Walkers. Walking notes: the A.A.A. Championships walk, Don Brown's illness, a 3 miles match win over Surrey Walking Club at Tooting Bec with full result, and prospects and notices for the road walking season; the printed result marks W. G. True (11th) as Belgrave but counts his place in Surrey W.C.'s score. Our walkers made a brave show in the A.A.A. Championships. Cooper won once again, with E. A. Staker (Highgate H.) 2nd. Harry Churcher was third, Percy Wright fourth, and Don Brown and Joe Coleman also finished inside first-class standard time. Len Coleman was just outside, and we had five men in the first eight places. We had hoped that Don Brown would beat A. A. Cooper (as he had done twice earlier in the season, in the "Kinnaird" race and Inter-Counties Championships), but after winning the London Business Houses title ten days previously he was taken ill and confined to bed with a severe chill. The after-effects were obviously still upon Don in the A.A.A. Championship, and it was noticeable from the first ten yards that he was not himself. So severe were the effects of the chill that Brown did not race again on the track after the Championships. However, he has now started again for the road season, and we trust he will have more luck in avoiding chills next season, and claim an A.A.A. Championship. * * * * * On July 6th we were invited by Surrey Walking Club to meet them in a 3 miles race at Tooting Bec Track. J. G. Coleman and N. A. L. Burt, of S.W.C., had a spirited tussle, but Joe,s speed and strength prevailed and he led us to a win. Scoring six aside, final points were Belgrave H. 34 pts., Surrey W.C. 44pts. * * * * * The Road season is with us again, and there is no reason why it should not equal in success our last record season. Our training and racing programme is on similar lines to previous years, and over a number of years we seem to have arrived at a programme which gets our men fit, and fit at the right time, which is of the greatest importance. We are sure that given the keenness and perseverance which are so essential, we shall continue to do well. * * * * * We shall again have out all those men who have brought the Club honour and distinction in recent years. It is most important, however, that we also have some new recruits with the necessary qualities; and we trust all our members will be on the look-out for youngsters likely to embrace the sport. We have some very promising younger members, but there is always room for more. Remember that we hold a novice race early in the season! * * * * * Can we win the "Junior" two seasons in succession? An affirmative answer depends upon the keenness of the eligible men. Bridger, Heather, Thaxter, Roberts, Doubleday, Snell, and others, supporting Bert Clayton, our Eastleigh member, who may win the individual title, is certainly a team of possibilities. However, March is a long way off yet; and we shall have further opportunities of discussing this very intriguing question. * * * * * The Southern Committee of the Road Walking Association are holding their Annual Supper on Monday, November 21st, at the Empire Restaurant, Victoria. It is for men only and the charge is 4/-. We hope Belgrave will be well represented. * * * * * All members will shortly be in possession of their fixture lists, and any member requiring further information, or wishing to enter any of the races, etc., should write to the Walking Hon. items.label: September 1938
items.sum: Report of Belgrave's annual inter-club walking contests at Battersea Park Track on June 8th, with results of the four miles, three miles, two miles and mile races and the final points table won by Belgrave.
items.s: The Annual Inter-Club Walking Contests. Report of Belgrave's annual inter-club walking contests at Battersea Park Track on June 8th, with results of the four miles, three miles, two miles and mile races and the final points table won by Belgrave. Our annual fixture was held at Battersea Park Track on June 8th, and again we had a splendid evening's sport. As Woodford Green A.C. and Valentine's S.C. had their own meetings on, they were unable to send teams along; but we were glad to welcome Cambridge Harriers and Highgate Harriers for the first time for some years. The first race was held at four miles (reduced from the usual five miles) and we were represented by R. F. Elson and C. E. Churcher. Harold Whitlock (Met. W.C.) won from Neilson, of the Poly. Our walkers finished third and sixth and gave us a lead on points. Our score was 25 points, while Highgate H. and Polytechnic H. scored 23 points each. RESULT. 1, H. H. Whitlock (Met. W.C.), 30m. 49s.; 2, H. D. Neilson (Poly H.), 31m. 22s.; 3, R. F. Elson (Bel. H.), 32m. 16s.; 6, C. E. Churcher (Bel. H.), 32m. 59s. Belgrave H., 25 pts.; Highgate H., 23 pts.; Polytechnic H., 23 pts.; London Vidarians W.C., 16 pts.; S.W.C., 14 pts.; Cambridge H., 7 pts. In the Three Miles race, Harry Churcher quickly took the lead and won comfortably from our second string, Jack Rutland, who is destined to be of great use to teams in future years. This, of course, gave us the maximum number of points, Surrey Walking Club being the next best scoring club. RESULT. 1, H. G. Churcher (Bel. H.), 23m. 12s.; J. E. Rutland (Bel. H.), 23m. 43s.; P. J. Reading (Poly H.), 23m. 52s. Belgrave H., 31 pts.; S.W.C., 25 pts.; Highgate H., 17 pts.; Polytechnic H., 14 pts.; London Vidarians W.C., 13 pts.; Cambridge H., 11 pts.; Surrey Athletic Club, 11 pts. In the Two Miles race Don Brown and Percy Wright were our representatives. They finished in first and third positions, M. J. Fisher, the Banks Champion and S.W.C. man, taking second place. Again we scored heavily in the competition with 30 points, Surrey W.C. taking 27 points. RESULT. 1, D. E. Brown (Bel. H.), 14m. 59s.; 2, M. J. Fisher (S.W.C.), 15m. 15s; 3, P. G. Wright (Bel. H.), 15 m. 28s. Belgrave H., 30 pts.; S.W.C., 27 pts.; Metropolitan W.C., 22 pts.; Cambridge H., 21 pts.; London Vidarians W.C., 15 pts. The final race of the evening, the Mile, saw another Belgrave walker victorious. Joe Coleman had a terrific battle with E. A. Staker, of Highgate H., and eventually won by a yard in 6 min. 56 sec. E. A. Heather, our other walker, finished fifth and so once again we piled up points. RESULT. 1, J. G. Coleman (Bel. H.), 6m. 56s.; 2, E. A. Staker (High. H.), 6m. 57s.; 3, A. H. items.label: September 1938
items.sum: Report on the London to Brighton walk, won by Tom Richardson, in which a depleted Belgrave team finished third, Colin Sutton (eighth) taking the Club Long Distance Championship and Belgrave Cup.
items.s: The Brighton Walk. Report on the London to Brighton walk, won by Tom Richardson, in which a depleted Belgrave team finished third, Colin Sutton (eighth) taking the Club Long Distance Championship and Belgrave Cup. This year's classic found us poorly represented, and it was evident that our team would do well to take third place; and that we had not one chance in a million of retaining our hold on the Shield. Circumstances combined to weaken our entry. Fred Bentley was, of course, in France representing Great Britain at the European Games. Jack Bidgood found the pressure of work in a new position prevented him from training. Jock Martin, a stalwart for many years in this race, was indisposed, as was also Fred Rickards. Readman and Roberts were also prevented from entering and we could only muster six entries against last year's eleven. Our great hope was Colin Sutton. Unfortunately, a severe cold laid him low a week before the race, necessitating a day in bed, but Colin started in this race as though in perfect health. At 18 miles he held a good lead, but the effects of the cold began to show and he fell back. Pluckily he carried on, despite a very bad time lasting for some hours, and eventually finished eighth in 8 hr. 44 min. 52 sec. Bill Urry, as last year, gave a splendid show of even walking and finished tenth in 8 hr. 56 min. 58 sec. He was the first "Service" athlete to finish and, as last year, won the special prize. Our third man, in 18th position, was Harry Thaxter. He completed the course in 9 hr. 11 min. 7 sec., and so gained a first-class standard medal. Thaxter is young in walking experience and is to be congratulated upon an excellent performance. Our team was completed by E. L. Reeve, a Club-champion at shorter distances some years back. Reeve, together with Don Willis and G. S. Doubleday, finished inside ten hours and so qualify for second-class team medals. Doubleday improved an hour and a half over the previous year's performance, which was incidentally his first walking race. The race for first position was one of the most exciting and interesting seen on the road for many years. Henderson, after taking the lead from Sutton, went well ahead and it seemed impossible to catch him. He was pegged back, however, and the leadership was continually changing. Eventually Tom Richardson (Woodford Green A.C.) who had created new World's Records the previous week at various distances, including twelve hours, came through to win in 8 hr. 8 min. 1 sec. At Crawley he had been over 10 minutes behind the leader. Leicester Walking Club were worthy winners of the Team contest, with the promoters, Surrey Walking Club, second, and ourselves third. Of the 93 entrants, 89 started and 75 finished—an excellent record! All our six entrants finished, and Colin Sutton won the Club Long Distance Championship and Belgrave Cup. Second and third medals go to Urry and Thaxter. Next year we hope to give better support to the race and place a stronger team on the road. Our team on this occasion did well—no one can be said to have walked below form—but we have others who would strengthen our representation. Perhaps next year will see some of our younger walkers making their first efforts in this annual race—one of the finest of sporting events—and in the Club Championship held in conjunction. Once again we thank in all sincerity those cyclist attendants who helped our men along—a feat of endurance, patience and self-sacrifice in itself. A Club bus was on the road and supporters, walkers and attendants travelled back together, tired but eager to be on the road again next year. items.label: September 1938
items.sum: Light verse by W. H. Snell celebrating Belgrave's walking season and its walkers and officials, introduced by an Hon. Editor's note.
items.s: Well Walked! Light verse by W. H. Snell celebrating Belgrave's walking season and its walkers and officials, introduced by an Hon. Editor's note. [Hon. Editor's Note.—Bill Snell is the first member for some while to burst into verse in our columns, and whilst his metre sometimes falters, and occasionally the rhyme is suspect, we congratulate him upon the sincerity of his lay, and the trouble he has taken. We should like other members to polish up their iambic pentameters, their dactyls and spondees, and maybe we shall find a Belgrave Laureate]. Congratulations to all you Belgrave men, The Coleman Brothers, Joe and Len. In the "Junior" they dead-heated, A hundred others were defeated. Sutton and Reg Elson completed the team, Smashed all records—they stand supreme. In all the "Sevens" and Valentine's "Ten," First scratch team were Belgrave men. Harry Churcher is the the "Champ" of them all, Of the many champions from Belgrave Hall. Six consecutive "Opens" has this chap won, A marvellous performance, never previously done. They went to Colchester to walk mile after mile, Our men smashing records in amazing style. Then up to Birmingham to contest the "Twenty," Our chaps showing stamina that they had in plenty. We've often been second, or sometimes third, But this time it's ours—at last!—I heard. Filling positions two, four, eight, and nine, They've won the Shield—"Excellent! Fine!" Bentley, Sutton, Bidgood and Rickards, At distance-walking, you know they are wizards. The "50 Kilos" at Bradford we won, Completing a "season" that takes the "bun." And now all praise to A. A. Harley, And our Captain, good old Charlie. Hard work they've done behind the scenes, Selecting the teams—you know what that means! They must feel proud of the work they've done, After seeing the Cups their teams have won. To all you youngsters this sounds very nice, But to get to the "top" take Harley's advice. To all new walkers, we start in September, From Belgrave Hall (a place to remember!) You may now be slow, but plug away, Hard training will get YOU first one day. Down to Roehampton, or round the "Hills," Keep with the "pack,' road sense it instils. In future years, you've lots to do, To uphold our prestige, and we're looking to YOU! W. H. SNELL. items.sum: Review of Belgrave's field events season: a fourth consecutive Southern Amateur Athletic League win, club championship records, and a tied field events match with Herne Hill H. (two printed team totals, 63ft. 3in. and 278ft. 4in., do not match the individual marks as printed).
items.s: Field Events. Review of Belgrave's field events season: a fourth consecutive Southern Amateur Athletic League win, club championship records, and a tied field events match with Herne Hill H. (two printed team totals, 63ft. 3in. and 278ft. 4in., do not match the individual marks as printed). The season just finished has been the most successful ever in the Club's history. For the fourth consecutive year we have won the Southern Amateur Athletic League competition, scoring 243 points. This represents eleven points out of a possible twelve from each event in which we have competed. Charlie Melchior did well to win the Javelin event in the "Waddilove Trophy" Competition at Birmingham—our only win—and so contributed in no small way towards the winning of the Bowl. In match events, too, our field events men have scored more points than our opponents, so helping our match wins. Club Championships Day saw records go in the High Jump, Shot Putt and Long Jump. Pack had an easy win in the High Jump clearing 5ft. 5in., and Skelley's 22ft. 8in. in the Long Jump compares favourably with performances in International matches. If he maintains this form next year he should gain his place in our national teams. S. Jones had an excellent win in the Shot Putt with 39ft. 1in.—the best performance yet in Club events by "home" talent—only Grassau and Pfenninger having beaten it. L. J. Worrad is the new Discus champion. He has recently joined us and has already proved himself a great asset. He was also second in the Weight (37ft. 0in.) and narrowly beaten for third place in the Long Jump, with 19ft. 10in. H. M. Quackenbos is the new Javelin holder. Melchior and Powell were unable to throw, owing to the claims of work, but Quack's win is the reward of persistence. When he matures physically, he will throw 160ft. At the Blackheath H. meeting at Motspur Park on August 20th, Melchior was third in a Javelin handicap. His scratch throw was 166ft., his best yet. We congratulate S. Jones upon winning the Shot Putt event in the Surrey and Middlesex match on August 27th. S.A.A.L. RESULTS. We were first on 11 occasions, second four times, third three times, fourth four times. Fourth was the lowest position ever occupied. On July 6th we had a Field Events match v. Herne Hill H. at Tooting Bec Track. A most enjoyable match ended in a tie, each Club winning three events. We hope to arrange more fixtures of this nature next season. Our Field Events men were prominent in the match v. London Associated Electrical Undertakings. Sutton won the Shot Putt, T. C. Jones the Long Jump, and Quackenbos the High Jump. At Charlton Park v. Cambridge H. our men were first and third in the High Jump (Quackenbos and Marchant); first and fourth in the Discus (Sutton and Jackson); first and fourth in Javelin (Quackenbos and Jackson); and second and fourth in the Long Jump (Skelley and "Q"). Other good work was done against the Old Rutlishians at Merton; and v. Southgate H. at Battersea. We would again emphasise the welcome awaiting new recruits to the Field Events side. In particular, we should be glad of some more High and Long jumpers. So if you know of anyone, please inform :— W. H. items.label: September 1938
items.sum: Club notes on summer matches, the juniors, relay and team wins, members' individual successes, club quarters, overseas readers and H. Parker's election to the Southern Counties Cross-country Association committee.
items.s: This And That. Club notes on summer matches, the juniors, relay and team wins, members' individual successes, club quarters, overseas readers and H. Parker's election to the Southern Counties Cross-country Association committee. A very pleasant evening was spent at Southfields on July 2nd, when we met Kensington Argyll A.C. We had an easy win and outstanding recollections are of Alf. Orton winning the 880 yards handicap, our Walking Hon. Secretary winning the Mile Walk Match, and of Albert Smith running a "slow-motion" half-mile in the Relay, which we won. Certainly, a very pleasant evening. * * * * * On July 18th we visited Merton and opposed Old Rutlishians A.C., who won the match. We received a fine welcome, enjoyed ourselves immensely and hope for a renewal of the very attractive fixture next season. * * * * * A club "B" team visited Norbury on July 7th, to meet London Associated Electrical Undertakings. We managed to win most things; and we understand our Track Captain will long remember being passed in the last few yards of the Mile! * * * * * Our Juniors, both in numbers and quality, have been very prominent this year, and we are confident that there is much first-class talent here. On July 6th, at Tooting Bec, they scored a very impressive win over the Juniors of Herne Hill H. and Mitcham A.C. * * * * * Our teams excelled themselves at the Ponders End Fête and Gala when we won two trophies. Our Relay team (Bird, Blunden, Pritchard, Pack) win in fine style; and our lads in the Three Miles race (Smart, Cohen, Carter) gave us another team win. * * * * * Stan Botwright has shown improved speed this season and his wins include the Civil Service 220 yards title, two B.W.S.A. titles, two Club titles and a medal in our second A.A.A. 4 x 440 yards Relay team. He also won the invitation 440 yards at the City Police Meeting off 12 yards in fast time and showed that he is capable of extending our best quarter-milers. * * * * * We are very glad to see Bert Footer "on the the road" again, and successful at High Wycombe (2nd), Plymouth (1st), Chiswick (1st) and in the British Workers' 10 miles Championship. We hope he carries this return of form on to the country and gets his place in the International team once again. Charlie Smart has been one of our most improved runners on the track and, now that he is eligible, will probably go near winning one of our Cross-Country Championships. He should be of great help to our cross-country teams when eligible—next season. * * * * * While Eddie Pack was away in Scotland again winning the Police 440 yards Championship, Cadogan A.C. strove to retain the Middlesex Relay title. The handicap of Pack's absence was too great, however, and although the team ran well, Highgate Harriers won the title. * * * * * On June 29th we were at Charlton Park opposing Cambridge Harriers. The track was in good condition—probably the best of the L.C.C. tracks—and in a match comprising running and field events and a walk, we won fairly easily. * * * * * Our quarters at Wimbledon are now open on Saturdays, and the mid-week quarters at "The Rising Sun," Ebury Bridge Road, on Tuesday and Thursday evenings. We urge all members to make the fullest use of the facilities provided. On race days, in particular, we would ask all non-active members to come along to Wimbledon and help with the arrangements, if necessary. You are always very welcome, and we like to have with us those who no longer turn out themselves, but retain (as we hope all our older members do) a keen interest in the Club's activities. * * * * * We have a letter from W. J. Ashford, now in Iran, in which he asks to be remembered to all friends in the Club. Our Gazette goes to Singapore, to Iran, to Bert Button, one-time member, in New South Wales, to a pre-war member now in New York; and it would be interesting to hear of other "long-distance" readers. * * * * * We are glad to know that H. Parker, who has served as President of the South of the Thames Association during the current athletic year, has been elected to the Committee of the Southern Counties Cross-country Association. We are sure our representation is in very capable hands, and that Harry's many years of experience will prove an asset to the Association. Alf. Orton Alf. Orton won the 880 yards handicap v. items.sum: Look back at club happenings of 1928: a North v. South track match, the first Griffin Cup, inter-club walks, the club championship winners and Harry Hare's re-election as President.
items.s: Ten Years Back. Look back at club happenings of 1928: a North v. South track match, the first Griffin Cup, inter-club walks, the club championship winners and Harry Hare's re-election as President. It is of the utmost interest to glance at the "Belgravian" of ten years ago, to re-live those days, and to know of the happenings of 1928! A track match was held between those living North of the Thames and those residing south of the river. Duffett managed the "South" team and Harley the "North" team, and an interesting match was won by the "North" by 4 events to 3. Among the Juniors running were T. H. Scrimshaw, T. C. Jones and T. F. Morrell. The Two Miles race was won by Bill Webb (N) narrowly from Bill Rice (S). All races were on team and relay principle and gave rise to great interest, and the present existence of Cadogan A.C. may be said to owe something to this meeting. The first Club championship for the "Griffin" Cup was held, and won by Jack Flower in 15 min. 21 sec. Duffett was second, and Micky Pyer third. At the same meeting Scrimshaw easily won an 880 yards handicap, off 40 yards, showing some of the form which was later to earn him International honours. The Inter-Club Scratch Walks of 1928 were won by Belgrave with 77 points; Ashcombe A.C. taking second place with 64 points. The Club Championships were won as follows: 100 yards, M. E. Odell (10.4 sec.); 440 yards, J. Cooper Clark (51 sec.); 880 yards, J. Cooper Clark (2 min. 1.6 sec.); Mile, T. J. Flower (4 m. 39.8 sec.); 2 miles Walk, R. D. McMullen (15 min. 4.4 sec.); 220 yards Junior, J. A. Ford (24.2 sec.). Some handicaps were included in the programme and were won as follows: 75 yards, E. Gordon; 880 yards, H. L. Rollins; 220 yards, Hurdles, T. C. Jones. It is noted that W. G. Webb won the "Fire Brigade" Mile, and at this time the identity of "Observer," who contributed notes regularly, was the cause of much enquiry and discussion. At the A.G.M. held in September, 1928, Harry Hare, who has served the Club in practically every capacity and also found time to score in Championship winning teams, was re-elected as President of the Club. These were the happenings of ten years ago! Duffett Duffett 1928: managed the "South" team; 2nd in first "Griffin" Cup championship Harley Harley 1928: managed the "North" team T. H. Scrimshaw T. H. items.sum: Notice of the 1938-39 social programme: two dances at the Ball Room, Zeeta House, Putney Hill, socials at Wimbledon, a Boxing Day Party and the Club Dinner fixed for May 7th, 1939 at The Empire Restaurant, Victoria.
items.s: Our Social Programme. Notice of the 1938-39 social programme: two dances at the Ball Room, Zeeta House, Putney Hill, socials at Wimbledon, a Boxing Day Party and the Club Dinner fixed for May 7th, 1939 at The Empire Restaurant, Victoria. Two Dances have been arranged to take place at The Ball Room, Zeeta House, Putney Hill, during the coming season. They are to be held on November 26th, 1938, and February 11th, 1939, and we have no doubt that our members will enjoy themselves at this newly-built hall. Situated at the junction of Putney Hill and Lower Richmond Road, almost on top of Putney Station (Southern Rly.) and served by many bus routes, our members should find it extremely easy of access. Socials at Wimbledon will be held on October 1st, October 22nd, December 10th, January 28th, and March 25th; and, in addition, we shall hold a Boxing Day Party, as last year. For the benefit of those who are marking up their 1939 diaries, the Club Dinner has been fixed for May 7th and will be held at The Empire Restaurant, Victoria. items.label: September 1938
items.sum: Report on the 1938 Inter-Club Relay Shield contests against Mitcham A.C., Epsom H. and Croydon H., which Belgrave won again with 63 points out of a possible 64.
items.s: The “Inter-Club” Relay Shield Contests. Report on the 1938 Inter-Club Relay Shield contests against Mitcham A.C., Epsom H. and Croydon H., which Belgrave won again with 63 points out of a possible 64. The second in this series was held at Croydon on May 31st, and we fielded quite a strong team and dropped only 1 point out of a possible 16. We won both the 4 x 100 yards and 4 x 300 yards relays, and then after a close and exciting race we also won the 4 x 880 yards. We were not so strongly represented in the 1 Mile team race, and Mitcham proved the winners of this with Bob Thorogood as the individual winner. The points scored that evening were : Belgrave H. 15, Mitcham A.C. 12, Croydon H 8, Epsom H. 5. On 13th July we visited Epsom for the third contest and once again the “turn-out” of our chaps was good to see. Unfortunately the same could not be said for our opponents and Mitcham were very weakly represented. The racing was more or less a procession, with our boys in front, and we won all four events. The points scored were : Belgrave H. 16, Mitcham A.C. 11, Epsom H. 7, Croydon H. 6. The final meeting was held at Mitcham on July 27th, and here again we scored maximum points in winning the four events down for decision. It was a pity that Mitcham did not put up a better fight on their own track, and they really have seemed very apathetic over the season’s contests. As regards Croydon and Epsom, we appreciate the hard fight they have in fielding teams; but from a club of Mitcham’s strength and reputation we expect keen opposition. If they cannot do better than this I am very much afraid their period of triumphs is nearing the end. We once again won the Shield, the final points being : Belgrave H. 63, Mitcham A.C. 46, Epsom H. 24, Croydon H. 20. As the highest possible is a total of 64 it will be seen we dropped only one point throughout the series of contests, a record which will stand for many years, and for which our boys deserve every congratulation. They rallied round in fine style and it was a great pity that our rivals did not take these contests in the same spirit. I trust that next season will see the same fine exciting battles that we have previously had for the possession of the Shield. Bob Thorogood Bob Thorogood individual winner of the 1 Mile team race, Croydon, May 31st Inter-Club Relay Shield Croydon Epsom Mitcham Mitcham A.C. Croydon H. Epsom H.

items.label: September 1938
items.sum: Report on the “Doris” Shield contest at Battersea Park Track on June 15th, won by Belgrave from Ashcombe-St. George's A.C. and Thames Valley Harriers despite a track in very bad condition. Handicap results for the 100 yards, 2 miles walk and 1 mile follow.
items.s: The “Doris” Shield Contest. Report on the “Doris” Shield contest at Battersea Park Track on June 15th, won by Belgrave from Ashcombe-St. George's A.C. and Thames Valley Harriers despite a track in very bad condition. Handicap results for the 100 yards, 2 miles walk and 1 mile follow. This season’s meeting was held at Battersea Park Track on June 15th and, as usual, the track was in a very bad condition. In fact, some of the athletes considered it dangerous to run on, and abstained from competing, which is to be regretted; and when things come to such a pitch as this it is high time the L.C.C. were asked to take this question in hand. The holders of the trophy were the Thames Valley Harriers and after making a very bad start in the 100 yards scratch race, they more or less gave up heart and did not compete in the final event. They took this stand on the condition of the track, and A. D. G. White, the Scottish International runner, was one of their members who refused to run. A. T. Liffen, of Ashcombe-St. George’s, won the 100 yards, with Stan Botwright and Tom Wiley filling the next two places. With the points scoring 6 down to 1 in each event, we thus got away to a flying start with 9 points from the first race. In the 440 yards Eddie Pack refused to risk a breakdown owing to the loose surface; and for an athlete of his build his point of view can be readily understood. Dick Michael made a fine substitute, however, and he ran well to beat Flynn of T.V.H., while Frank Webb sportingly turned out and gained points by finishing 4th. The 2 Miles Team race resulted in an easy win for our team and they actually finished abreast in first position. Our three were : Les Cohen, Tom Carter and Charlie Smart, and their time of 9 min. 56 sec. was very good, bearing in mind the state of the track. For the final event, the 1 Mile Relay, Thames Valley H. did not field a team, and we won after a good race with Ashcombe-St. George’s A.C. The final points for the Shield were : Belgrave H. 30, Ashcombe-St. George’s A.C. 21, Thames Valley H. 12. As usual at this meeting, we had three handicap events open to members of the competing clubs. In the 100 yards there were many absentees and with one heat a walk-over, and some of the others with two or three runners only, we had a final of 5 runners—all “Bels.” F. W. Pritchard (5) won a good race with R. B. Shepherd (8) second, and S. Lyons (4) third in 10.3 secs. The 2 Miles Walk proved another good race and a promising young walker in A. E. Elliott (475) was the winner with S. Mable (575) second, and W. True (550) third. These are all long-markers but the rest of the field was very close up. A good field was seen out in the 1 Mile handicap, and here a visitor in W. F. Gant, of T.V.H., off 130 yards, ran a well-judged race to run home a good winner. R. W. Tobin, of Belgrave, off 100, was second and Bert Cook, better known as a Poly Harrier, was third off 110 yards. A. D. G. White A. D. G. items.label: September 1938
items.sum: Report on the Kinnaird Trophy meeting at the Polytechnic Harriers' new ground at Chiswick, won by Achilles with Belgrave fifth on 12 points, with Tom Carter second in the Southern Counties 2 Miles Steeplechase, a Belgrave team win in the Invitation 2 Miles Walk and Belgrave finishers in the Marathon.
items.s: The “Kinnaird Trophy” Meeting. Report on the Kinnaird Trophy meeting at the Polytechnic Harriers' new ground at Chiswick, won by Achilles with Belgrave fifth on 12 points, with Tom Carter second in the Southern Counties 2 Miles Steeplechase, a Belgrave team win in the Invitation 2 Miles Walk and Belgrave finishers in the Marathon. We were once again honoured by receiving an invitation to compete at this meeting, which was held at the fine new ground of the Polytechnic Harriers at Chiswick. As usual our boys gave a very creditable display in being placed fifth in the list of competing clubs which included all of any note. Achilles, with their formidable list of talent to draw on—far in excess of any that an ordinary club can command—were easy winners of the trophy with a total of 71 points. Highlights of the meeting so far as we were concerned were Stan Botwright’s fine running in the 220 yards, and in his heat he caused a surprise by beating J. C. Horsfall, of Achilles Club. In the final he was placed 4th, and so scored 3 points. Another fine performance was Eddie Pack’s running in the 440 yards, and after an easy heat win, he made A. G. K. Brown go all the way in the final. Eddie was leading at 300 yards, but once the straight was reached Brown forged ahead, and Eddie was also “pipped” on the tape for second place by C. H. Kearney, the American running for Achilles. It was one of Pack’s best runs to date and if he could only find something of a finish, I would back him against the best in the country. In the 880 yards Alby Bird ran his usual consistent race and although coming up against his “bogey” man, A. D. G. White, in his heat they both managed to qualify for the final. This was a fine race and White proved the winner, just beating J. V. Powell, with Bird in third place. These three runners had so far scored 11 points for us, which was in excess of any number scored previously by us in these contests, and then Charlie Smart, by gaining 6th place in the 3 Miles, brought our totai to 12. At this meeting was held the Southern Counties 2 Miles Steeplechase and although the water jump was far from satisfactory, after some discussion it was decided to hold the race. Tom Carter put up very good and plucky show and after Abberton, of Q.P.H.—he is also a member of the “Bels”—had led most of the way Tom looked like making up the lost ground with a lap to go. Then, bad luck, Tom hit a hurdle and fell and although still retaining second place, he found it impossible to catch the leader. In the Invitation 2 Miles Walk, the Belgrave boys gave the fair sized crowd a good example of the heel and toe “stuff” and Don Brown walked in his best style to beat A. A. Cooper, the A.A.A. champion. Joe Coleman was third, and with Harry Churcher, Percy Wright, Len Coleman and J. E. Rutland giving good support, we scored an easy win in the team race by scoring 13 pts. to Surrey Walking Club’s 39, four aside scoring. In the Marathon, F. A. Walker and A. F. Mitchell ran well to gain first class standards; and Bert Lindsey and F. G. White finished the course and completed our team. Stan Botwright Stan Botwright 4th, 220 yards final (3 points); beat J. C. items.label: September 1938
items.sum: Report of the club 3 Miles Track Championship for the “Griffin” Cup at Battersea Park on June 22nd, won by Tom Carter in 15 min. 12 sec. from the holder Les Cohen, with standard medals, the evening's handicap results, an unattached novices' race and a schools' relay.
items.s: Club 3 Miles Championship Meeting. Report of the club 3 Miles Track Championship for the “Griffin” Cup at Battersea Park on June 22nd, won by Tom Carter in 15 min. 12 sec. from the holder Les Cohen, with standard medals, the evening's handicap results, an unattached novices' race and a schools' relay. At Battersea Park, on June 22nd, we held an evening meeting and included on the programme was our 3 Miles Track Championship for the “Griffin” Cup. The holder, Les Cohen, was among the starters who were quite numerous, although Pat Parker, owing to his domicile, was an absentee. The first mile was reached in 5 min. 2 sec., the second in 10 min. 14 sec., and the leading bunch included all the Club’s most prominent distance runners. Over the final lap Cohen was in the lead with Tom Carter next; and Les still kept in front until half-way down the finishing straight, when Tom made a do-or-die effort, and won a fine race in 15 min. 12 sec. Dan Patience beat Charles Smart for third place, while other runners to gain 1st class standard medals were Rod Patience, Syd Ring, Alf Taylor and Dick Tobin. Second class standards were gained by Afthur Allum, Tom Morrell, R. E. Stride and E. H. Herbert. Also on the programme were several handicap events, and in the 100 yards Junior race R. B. Shepherd (2) beat G. Morgan (3), there being only four starters. The Unattached Novices race, over 100 yards, was won by R. Bradshaw in 11.3 sec. with G. Aylmer and F. Wood next. In the 880 yards race, a Junior in D. L. Mumford (off 72 yards) showed his paces in winning in quite fast time and, as he is finely built, he should prove a most useful addition to our ranks. Syd Jarlett ran a fine race in being second off 28 yards (his improvement this season has been remarkable) and R. J. Powell, off 60 yards, made one of his few appearances on the track, to take third place. We also had a 1 Mile Relay, open to Schools, and were rather disappointed in that only two teams took part in this. Latymer Upper School easily beat Sloane School, to take the first awards, thus repeating last year’s success. I hope that if we hold this event next season we shall gain a much better entry. In the Club Shot Putt handicap, the winner was Frank Webb. Now I know how he gets the nickname of “Snaky,” and he did 37ft. 5½in. with 15ft. start. None other than Percy Wright was second and he did 37ft. 3¾in. off 15ft. 3in., while Joe Coleman was third with 37ft. 0½in. The 100 Yards Veterans’ race was won by J. Smith (6), who beat E. R. Jessop (8), with Dicky Best (7) third. In the 2 Miles Walk an old-time member, in A. H. East, made a return to something like his old form to win off the 550 yards mark. E. G. Cornish (425) was second, with Reg Elson (225) walking well to gain third place. The 220 yards handicap saw R. B. Shepherd win a good race off 16 yards, with Bill Pritchard, off 8 yards, second, and Syd Jarlett (12) gaining another success by being third. The Club Long Jump handicap was won by H. M. Quackenbos (3ft. 6in.) with 21ft. 3in., Charlie Jones and Bill Pritchard gaining the other places. We saw quite a promising runner in the 1 Mile run for Unattached Novices in C. Westwood, who has now joined us. He won in confident style, and should prove a useful addition to our ranks of distance runners. items.label: September 1938
items.sum: Report on Belgrave's win in the Stanley Waddilove Trophy contest at the Birchfield Harriers ground, Perry Barr, on July 23rd, by 13 points to 12 each for London A.C., Blackheath H. and Birchfield H., decided by the final relay on the grass.
items.s: The “Waddilove” Trophy Contest. Report on Belgrave's win in the Stanley Waddilove Trophy contest at the Birchfield Harriers ground, Perry Barr, on July 23rd, by 13 points to 12 each for London A.C., Blackheath H. and Birchfield H., decided by the final relay on the grass. Once again we journeyed to Birmingham to take part in this meeting at the Birchfield Harriers ground at Perry Barr. Last year, at our first time of competing, we managed to share the trophy with the London A.C., but with the Blackheath H. sending up a strong side, which included Sidney Wooderson, we were not too optimistic this time. Further, Eddie Pack was in Belfast running for England in the triangular match there, and so lessened our chance of picking up points in the 440 yards event. Anyway, a very cheerful party under the guidance of our Running Hon. Sec. met at Euston Station on the morning of July 23rd and duly arrived at Perry Barr prepared to do their best. In the 100 yards Ted Gray, as last year, won his heat and so gained a place in the final. Wiard, of Blackheath, as expected, won the final and although close up, Ted was placed 4th, which was not so good as previously. We had a surprise in the 440 yards, inasmuch as both our runners won their heats, and so we had two in the final. Dick Michael and Syd Jarlett were our two stalwarts, but on a very loose track G. N. Blake won for the L.A.C., with Neal and Lansdale, both of Birchfield, in the next two places. Jarlett was inches away in 4th place. Thus we gained another very valuable point and with the 880 yards next, we hoped for the best from Alby Bird. Wooderson made his first appearance in this race and as the field also included J. V. Powell, J. W. Alford (the Empire Games champion) and many other first-class runners, all the crowd were agog with excitement. After a very bumpy start, Wooderson shot to the front and was not again headed, beating Jack Powell, while Alby Bird ran magnificently to beat Alford on the tape for third place. The time of 2 mins. 0.6 secs. came rather as an anti-climax, but no doubt the state of the track coupled with the presence of Wooderson, slowed the field down somewhat. Meanwhile in the centre of the arena the Javelin Throw was proceeding, this event being an innovation as regards this contest. We had Charlie Melchior throwing for us, but with Blakeway and Klein entered for Achilles, our man appeared outclassed. Imagine our surprise when Melchior nonchalantly walked up to us and said he had won the Javelin. It transpired that only three competitors turned out, and these did not include either of the Achilles men, and so Charlie with a throw of 151 ft. beat J. W. P. Ellis, of the L.A.C., with J. Cotter, of Birchfield, next. Thus on points scored we were well among the leaders and our hopes of success were gradually rising. The 2 Miles Team race was next, and although we provided the winning team last year we were much weaker on this occasion. Also the field was a really “hot” one, the Achilles team being Ward, McIntyre and Ellis, while the Poly. had Reeve, Furze and Stockwell, and there were, of course, the Birchfield boys to be considered. Our team, owing to withdrawals, was Charlie Smart, Bill Lucas, Alf Taylor, with our track captain, Harry Shields, making a fourth man. After a very fine race Reeve beat Ward on the post to win a most plucky race in which Ward appeared to make his effort rather late, although I do not think he bargained for the way Reeve fought him off down the straight. Achilles scored 16, to the Polytechnic’s 18 to win the team race, and after much speculation we heard with pleasure that we were third with 32, to Birchfield’s 38. Charlie Smart ran another good race, employing his forcing tactics to take the field along at a good pace, but, as usual, he could not match their pace over the final lap. Bill Lucas, running over his usual distance, did quite well, and Alf Taylor was our third man. So with one event to go we found ourselves in a similar position to last year, We just had to beat the L.A.C. and Birchfield, for the latter were in the lead by one point from ourselves and the L.A.C. As by this time the track was very cut up, the competing clubs asked the officials if they could use the grass for this event. It had been marked out for a previous race, so that it was quite easy to arrange the take-overs, etc., and it was agreed to run on the grass. Sidney Wooderson turned out for Blackheath over the two laps stage, and duly handed over in the lead; but Alby Bird had hunted him home and we were in second place. Syd Jarlett kept us well there and then Stan Blundell went off over the first half lap, and Stan Botwright took over for the final run home. Wiard was leading for Blackheath but Botwright caught him at the bend of the home straight. The Blackheath man was the stronger, however, and beat our runner by a yard or so; with the L.A.C. just beating Birchfield for third place. Oh ! boys ! what a finish ! This had given us the Cup, the final points being : Belgrave H. 13, and then with 12 points came London A.C., Blackheath H. and Birchfield H. Polytechnic H. scored 5, and the Achilles 4 points. Were our lads excited? And it was very gratifying to find the locals were also very pleased at the “Bels” success. After a very nice tea we entrained for home and all that goes with it, and so ended yet another page in the Club’s history—winners of the Stanley Waddilove Trophy ! items.s: Match v. Southgate Harriers. Report of the July 20th match at Battersea Park Track in which Belgrave's Seniors beat Southgate Harriers 42 pts. to 38 and the Juniors won a match against Mitcham A.C., Hercules A.C. and Croydon H, with club handicaps and a Mile Novices Walk on the same programme. On July 20th we had as visitors to Battersea Park Track the Southgate Harriers, who met our Seniors in a series of match events. The Milocarian A.C. had also been invited and after accepting, they found at the last minute it was impossible to raise a full team. Actually one of their members came all the way from Portsmouth to compete and was very disappointed at their withdrawal. Our Juniors was also entertaining the junior members of the Croydon H., Hercules A.C. and Mitcham A.C. In the Senior 100 yards Southgate proved too strong for us; but Alby Bird credited us with first place in the 880 yards, and Frank Webb ran a fine race, to gain third place in this event. We had the first two in the Shot Putt with S. Jones and L. J. Worrad; and in the 220 yards Stan Blunden ran a fine race, only to lose first place by inches to S. C. Francis, of Southgate. Another good race was the 1 Mile match and B. S. Cornish, of Southgate, proved the winner, after running a very well-judged race. Bill Lucas chased him home and appeared to have left his effort too late, while Les Cohen filled 3rd position. The 440 yards saw Dick Michael run a smashing race to beat Syd Jarlett, with the Southgate men well in the rear. Points which were scored 4, 3, 2, 1, were equally shared in the Discus Throw, and also the 2 Miles, which E. J. Nankivell, of the visitors, won in good style and quite good time. Thus the Senior match ended with Belgrave H. 42 pts., and Southgate H. 38 pts. The Junior match was also very well contested and some fine running was seen, one of the best performances being J. A. W. Scott’s double in the 100 yards and 220 yards. Scott is quite a “find” for us and should develop into a really fine sprinter. In the 880 yards the winner was J. Emmins, of the Hercules A.C., one of the best juniors in the South and our boys did well in gaining third and fourth places. Our “dusky” member, C. Holloway, gained 4th place in the High Jump and with proper tuition he should do even better. A fine race was seen in the 440 yards and G. H. Knight scored a win for us by battling up the straight to win the race on the tape. D. R. Laing also showed good form in being placed 4th and here again we have two extremely promising young runners. In the final event, the 1 Mile Relay, the Hercules team kept the lead given them by Emmins and our team were also always in second place, the Mitcham boys being third. The points for the Junior match were : Belgrave H. 22, Mitcham A.C. 19, Hercules A.C. 14, Croydon H. 5. Also on this programme were a few club handicaps, one being the 100 yards for Boys under 16. We had quite a good entry and the final was won by A. P.Norris (2), who beat A. V. Heitman (Scr.), with P. Kearney, Jnr. (2) third. In the 2 Miles Walk handicap, A. H. East scored another win, this time off 450 yards, and it would appear his long rest has done him the world of good. W. Brunning, a very persevering member, was second (off 775) and J. Ogilvie (off 500) was placed third. The 220 yards was won by Stan Blunden off 8 yards, with Dick Michael (12) second, and Alec Mewes (11) third. Blunden is another runner to show remarkable improvement this season and if he can only improve his rather ungainly style he should still further increase his speed. In the Mile handicap a good race was seen and although Joe Daly fought hard to keep in front he eventually finished third, with Alf Taylor beating J. T. Beer for first place. The latter has also shewn gradual improvement and now that he is out of the Junior ranks he should soon be knocking at the door of our Senior teams. We also held a Mile Novices Walk, but the entry was poor; although the winner, J. Howard, showed a good style in winning by quite a distance. Alby Bird Alby Bird won the Senior 880 yards v. items.s: The Club Championships. G. S. Doubleday reports the Belgrave club championships at Tooting Bec Track on Saturday, July 30th, with the full results appended; the report puts Bill Sutton third in the Discus behind Worrad and Jones, while the results list W. H. J. Sutton second and S. Jones third, and the report gives Jones’ javelin as 131ft .1in. where the results print 131ft. 1in. These were held at Tooting Bec Track on Saturday, July 30th, on a brilliant summer afternoon; a fair-sized crowd and many club-folk enjoyed the sport. The heats of the 100 yards were held first. Owing to a small field the final of the Boy’s Sprint was held straight away, J. McLean winning from P. Kearney, and A. V. Heitman (holder), in 11.4 secs. Meanwhile, the Shot Putters were “toying” with the 16lb. ball. Sid Jones came out best with an effort of 39ft. 1in. L. J. Worrad and Bill Sutton were 2nd and 3rd, with 37ft. and 34ft. 9in. respectively. No standards (31ft.) were gained here. Then the Juniors lined up for their 880 yards. D. Mumford showed good judgment to win from L. Marchant, and N. Shrubb in 2 min. 7 1-6 sec. This served as an appetiser for the Senior 880 yards, in which Alby Bird (holder) went into the lead at once, with the rest closely behind. At the bell he showed us that he meant to retain his title, and spurted ahead to enter the final straight with a commanding lead to win in 2 min. 3sec. Dick Michael led the others at the last bend and looked as though he would be runner-up, but Sid Jarlett had other ideas, fought him down the straight, and just “pipped” him. Standards (2 min. 8 sec.) were gained by F. H. C. White, F. R. Webb and A. H. Orton. Next came the 100 yards Finals. In the Junior, R. S. Turner won in 10.8 sec., a time which is very encouraging for one under 19. J. A. W. Scott and R. B. Shepherd were 2nd and 3rd. These lads will, I’m sure, soon be forcing themselves into the Club’s Senior teams. In the Senior race, Stan Botwright gained a clear victory in the excellent time of 10.2 sec. over F. Skelley, who was chased home by Tom Wiley. F. Pritchard was the other finalist. The Field Events men had now deserted the Shot for the Discus. This gave us a close finish, Worrad reversing the previous result with Jones (holder) and winning by a foot. Bill Sutton was again third, the distances being 100ft. 7in., 99ft. 7in. and 92ft. 11in. No Standards (85ft.) were obtained. The sprinters were again on the tracks now, deciding who were to line up for the 220 yards final. Our attention was then drawn to the High Jump, which was won by a member whose name is not usually associated with jumping—Eddie Pack. He cleared 5ft. 5in., and a junior, Len Marchant, was second with 5ft. 3in.; he will undoubtedly get higher, as his physique is well suited to this event. H. M. Quackenbos (holder) cleared 5ft. 2in. for 3rd place. The absence of Les Cohen and Pat Parker robbed the Mile of some of its interest, but an exciting race between W. Lucas and L. W. Herbert held the attention of us all. Lucas led the way right from the start, Herbert being content with keeping just behind. Thus they went until the bell, having dropped the rest on the last lap. Herbert attacked down the back straight. Lucas held him for a while, but on entering the final straight Herbert put in a powerful finish which Lucas could not quite resist. This is not only Herbert’s first Club Championship win, but a new Club record of 4 min. 29.2 sec. The field were battling for third place, Charlie Smart proving the best of the bunch. Standards (4 min. 50 sec.) were gained by Dan Patience, Ted Stimpson, Alf Taylor, Tom Morrell, Tom Carter, Harry Shields and Syd Ring. Then the 220 yards finalists lined up and the Juniors again gave us a keen race. In a very good time—23.8 sec.—R. B. Shepherd led R. S. Turner and J. A. W. Scott. Stan Botwright again showed the others a clean pair of heels, winning in 22.7 sec. (new Club record) while A. S. Blunden, F. W. Pritchard and Tom Wiley—finishing in that order—gave us a close race. Eddie Pack, Alec Mewes, S. Lyons and Les Bennett gained Standards (24 sec.) in their heats. In the absence of C. Melchior, G. Powell and E. H. Finneron, the Javelin resolved itself into a close contest between Quackenbos and S. Jones, the former winning with 133ft. 2in. and Jones throwing 131ft .1in. I’m sure that Quackenbos’ prowess is chiefly due to a close study of the finer points of Javelin throwing. A rather small number lined up for the Two Miles Walk. Harry Churcher and Joe Coleman led from the start, with Percy Wright in close attendance until he incurred the Judge’s displeasure. Len Coleman and Bill Treacher were battling for third place until Treacher was disqualified at 1½ miles. Harry was a little too fast for Joe, and won in 14 min. 36 sec. Reg Elson followed home to gain a First Class Standard, but no other Standards were obtained. The holder, D. Brown, did not start, and I am sure that his presence in the race would have added considerable interest. The last race was the 440 yards final. As was expected, Eddie Pack had a comfortable win, and cantered home in 51.6 sec. Sid Jarlett again gave us a fighting finish to beat Alby Bird and Dick Michael. Jarlett’s improved running has been one of the features of the season. A. H. Orton gained another Standard, having beaten 56 sec. in his heat. Meanwhile F. Skelley had jumped 22ft. 8in. to retain his Long Jump title. This is surely one of the best jumps by an Englishman this season. T. D. Wiley and F. W. Pritchard were second and third. No account would be complete without a hearty vote of thanks and a strong recommendation for a big drink and a box of throat tablets for our Hon. Announcer, Arthur Cook, who gave us a sterling performance on the megaphone. Our other officials, too, deserve warmest thanks from both competitors and spectators. Last, but not least, we thank the competitors whose performances will, no doubt, urge them on in quest of greater honours—sufficient unto the day is the attainment thereof. items.sum: Report of the club handicap events at the final evening meeting at Battersea Park on August 10th.
items.s: The Final Evening Meeting. Report of the club handicap events at the final evening meeting at Battersea Park on August 10th. As usual, we held an evening meeting at Battersea Park in August and on the 10th we held the following handicap events. This year we experimented with a 300 yards race, but entries were very poor, due mainly to holidays, and Alby Bird, off 10 yards, ran a good race to just beat Stan Blunden, off 6. Tom Wiley (8) was third while among the also rans was—yes, that man’s here again—Percy Wright. In the Shot Putt “that man,” or in other words, P. G. Wright, was the winner with 38ft. 11in. He received 15ft. 6in. R. Stride, Snr. (16ft. 6in.) did 38ft. 4in., while Alby Bird (15ft. 6in.) gained third prize after dead-heating with the scratch man, S. Jones, both doing 38ft. 3in. As Jones did 39ft. 1in. in our Club Championships, a repetition of this would have gained him first place. A good race was seen in the 880 yards Junior handicap and L. Marchant made good use of his 10 yards allowance to beat N. C. Shrubb (15) for first place. Our Junior champion, D. L. Mumford, was third off the scratch mark. These three juniors are three extremely promising young runners, and Shrubb was recently selected to represent the Surrey Juniors. The 2 Miles Walk saw a rather small field and Charlie Speechley (450) scored a popular win, with A. H. East, off a much reduced mark, still keeping among the prize winners by being second off the 330 yards mark. Reg Elson walked in his usual fluent style to gain third place with 190 yards start. Harry Churcher walked well from the scratch mark and eventually worked his way through to 4th place. A popular distance with our lads is the 2 Miles race and Ted Stimpson showed he is working back to his best form by winning off 100 yards; while Tommy Morrell (160) ran well to gain second place. Frank Webb (170) was third. To Frank it would appear that the distance is immaterial, be it anything from 300 yards to 10 miles. Another feature of this race was the fine running of L. W. Herbert who, off 50 yards went through the field in fine style and only lost third place in the last few strides. He just failed to overtake Frank Webb, and as the time of the race was 9 min. 30 sec., Herbert must have been doing fast time as he was close up to the leaders at the finish. items.s: The Forthcoming Winter Season. Preview of the 1938-39 winter season: training at Belgrave Hall, Wimbledon and the mid-week quarters at the "Rising Sun", Ebury Bridge Road, and the autumn fixtures. The piece ends at the foot of printed page 28 (scan p.30) without a sign-off, but the printed page numbers run unbroken from 1 to 28 and are followed by the blank back covers, so no pages are missing from the scan. After one of our most successful Summer seasons ever, we look forward with confidence to the forthcoming Winter season. We have arranged a full fixture list and I trust our members will give the fixtures their fullest support, both at home and away. We are also extremely fortunate in possessing our own hall—Belgrave Hall—at Wimbledon and here again the Common is ideal for running purposes. I hope all members, both new and old, will come along to Wimbledon and sample the delights of a run over the country, there is nothing better for getting rid of that “tired” feeling, never mind what the advertisements say! We have a fine bath of hot water for use after the run, and our capable masseur, Tom Easton, is also in attendance, if required. Saturday runs always start about 3 p.m. and for those who would like to do some mid-week training we have our quarters at the rear of the “Rising Sun,” Ebury Bridge Road, which is quite near Victoria Station. We go out from here every Tuesday and Thursday evening and run over the adjacent roads into Hyde Park, when we go round Rotten Row, which makes for very useful country training, especially if we have had some rain, and then back to the quarters. Hot water can also be obtained here and while conditions are not quite so ideal as at Wimbledon it must be borne in mind that suitable mid-week quarters, especially in this vicinity, are extremely difficult to obtain. Now a word as to our fixtures. On the first Saturday in October (which is October 1st) we hold our annual 3 Miles Road Run and 5 Miles Road Walk. Both these events are handicap races and all members have an equal chance of success, so be sure to enter in good time. The following week, October 8th, we hold the usual Novice races open to Unattached men, and also members of our own Club. If you have any friends who would like to try their paces, bring them along to Wimbledon on this day. We are then away to Ealing Harriers, and then on the 22nd we have a home fixture with London University C.C.C. In conjunction with this race we shall hold our usual 5 Miles handicap. We expect to have a good field out. This season we visit Cranford for the annual Inter-Club race with Thames Valley H. and Ashcombe-St. Georges A.C., the date being October 29th. Then on November 5th we make our first visit to Aldershot for a run with the Aldershot Command team. We are also paying a visit to Cambridge for a run with the University Hare and Hounds and in each case a picked team will represent the Club. items.label: December 1938
items.sum: The secretary's notes on the vote of thanks to W. L. Bayliss on his retirement as Hon. Secretary, the club's answer to a press claim that athletics was unknown in Wimbledon, members' marriages, the R.W.A. 20 Miles team in the Lord Mayor's Show, Harry Churcher's walking form, cross-country hopes and the Winter Handbook.
items.s: The Hon. Secretary's Commentaries. The secretary's notes on the vote of thanks to W. L. Bayliss on his retirement as Hon. Secretary, the club's answer to a press claim that athletics was unknown in Wimbledon, members' marriages, the R.W.A. 20 Miles team in the Lord Mayor's Show, Harry Churcher's walking form, cross-country hopes and the Winter Handbook. Every member will endorse the Vote of Thanks which was accorded to W. L. Bayliss at the Annual General Meeting, when he announced his retirement from the office of Honorary Secretary. It was framed in the following terms, proposed by W. H. Hare :— “That this meeting place on record its very grateful thanks and appreciation for the services rendered to the Belgrave Harriers by Mr. W. L. Bayliss as the Hon. Sec. during the past eleven years. His unfailing efforts to further the development and welfare of the Club in all its activities have materially assisted in the acquisition of every Road and Cross Country Team Honour in the Athletic World. In addition, his services have been of the greatest assistance in obtaining the leasehold of our own Headquarters. We feel that no Hon. Secretary has retired with as great a measure of satisfaction of service rendered to our Club and we both congratulate and thank most heartily Wally Bayliss for his sterling efforts on our behalf.” A. A. Harley said that such a proposition required no seconder but was rather the expression of feeling of every member present, and upon formally placing the motion before the meeting it was received and passed with acclamation. As President of the Club for the third successive year, we are assured that there will be no diminution in his interest, or in his labours on the Club's behalf. His experience gained in close upon twenty years' membership of the Club will still be ours to draw upon, and his enthusiasm for all aspects of the Club's activities will remain an example to all members. * * * * * We note from the Press that a Wimbledon Athletic Club has been formed, and shall watch its progress with interest. Naturally, we take the broad view and welcome any new organisation likely to bring newcomers into the ranks of Athletics, and extend the influence of our sport among a new section of the public. We must confess, however, to some slight annoyance at reading the “blurb” which appeared in one of our national papers and accompanied the announcement of the formation of the new club. From this it would appear that Wimbledon has only been known hitherto in sporting circles by reason of its association with Lawn Tennis. No doubt the Royal Wimbledon Golf Club and Wimbledon F.C., to name only two sporting bodies, would be inclined to dispute this; and we certainly think we have some claim to have brought some small Athletic distinction to the Borough of Wimbledon. For many years now we have been privileged to train at Wimbledon, and it would be no exaggeration to say that the Cross-country and Road Walking titles we have gained have been won, in part, on the Common and roads of Wimbledon, in advance of the Championship events. On nineteen occasions we have promoted an Open Walk at Wimbledon, attracting an average entry of 200 walkers. Last season we invited French athletes to Wimbledon for the first time ever, as far as we know, and the Mayor and members of the Corporation honoured us by officiating at these events and congratulated the Club upon its efforts for Athletics. We are minor property owners and ratepayers in Wimbledon, and our quarters have been at the disposal of the Wimbledon “Keep Fit” movement and other sporting organisations—and yet we are told that Athletics is an unknown sport in Wimbledon! So much for Press reports. We are content to carry on in a placid way, doing what we can for athletes and Athletics, wherever we can, achieving Championship honours or failing honourably to do so; and leave the verdict to those who have an intimate knowledge of all the facts, and ignore the inaccurate vapourings of ill-informed hearsay. * * * * * Congratulations to C. W. Redgrave and F. H. C. White upon their recent marriages. We wish both these popular members many years of happiness. * * * * * The appearance in the recent Lord Mayor's Show of the winning team in the R.W.A. 20 Miles Championship and the Hon. Secretary—representing Road Walking—was an honour to the Club. These five members paraded in Club track suits in the Athletics section of the National Fitness Campaign pageant, which was the central motif of this year's Show. * * * * * Harry Churcher is again showing his heels to all other walkers. We congratulate him upon the excellence of his form, and trust he will be equally successful in the races still to come. Our teams are also pre-eminent at the moment, and we confidently anticipate that their series of successes will continue. * * * * * Our runners are training steadily and showing up well in inter-club events, and are certain to give a good account of themselves when the Championship season arrives. Every club member hopes the team will be free of injury and indisposition during the coming months, and successfully bid for the English Cross-country Championship next March, to be held near Manchester. * * * * * All members should now have their Winter Handbook containing Winter fixtures and Rules. Anyone who has not received his copy should get into touch with the Hon. Secretary. * * * * * W. L. Bayliss W. L. Bayliss retired as Hon. Secretary after eleven years; President for the third successive year Mr. W. L. Bayliss Wally Bayliss Wally Bayliss W. H. Hare W. H. Hare proposed the vote of thanks at the Annual General Meeting A. items.s: Letter from A. A. Harley, editor since April 1929, wishing the new editor luck and thanking F. R. Webb and E. A. Duffett for their support. 39, Roxborough Avenue, Isleworth, Mx. Dear Mr. Editor, May I trespass on your space to wish you the Best of Luck with “The Belgravian,” and plenty of support from all members in the position to which you have been appointed by the Committee? It was in April, 1929, that I succeeded Ben Knifton as Hon. Editor, and during the intervening years I have had the pleasure of presenting 59 issues to an increasing membership, and have had the honour of recording Belgrave victories in practically every team championship and race of any importance. I trust it will be your good fortune to continue to record success after success, and to give written expression to the wonderful spirit within the Club that has created these successes and the good-fellowship which is so real to all of us. In conclusion, I should like to thank all who have co-operated with me during the past nine years in my Editorial efforts, particularly F. R. Webb and E. A. Duffett, two stalwarts who have always given me invaluable support. I am sure that we may expect many fine “Belgravians” under your direction, and that we shall all eagerly await each quarter the results of your labours. And so, good editing! Sincerely yours, A. A. HARLEY. A. A. Harley A. A. HARLEY Hon. Editor from April 1929, 59 issues Ben Knifton Ben Knifton Hon. Editor before April 1929 F. R. Webb F. R. Webb E. A. Duffett E. A. Duffett Isleworth

items.label: December 1938
items.sum: The new Hon. Editor introduces himself, invites members' articles alongside sectional reports, and notes that A. A. Harley will continue to contribute.
items.s: From The Hon. Editor. The new Hon. Editor introduces himself, invites members' articles alongside sectional reports, and notes that A. A. Harley will continue to contribute. Having been appointed by the Committee to be Editor of your magazine, I feel that I would like to write a few words in my first issue. I write “your Magazine” because it is your magazine, written about you and for you, and it is by no means an unimportant phase of the Club's activities with which I must confess a little pride in being associated. I don't think that any other athletic club can lay claim to a publication of the size of “The Belgravian.” However, being what we are (if you don't know that, I will ask you to turn to the letter from A. A. Harley, in which he sums the Club up in a few well-chosen and appropriate words), the publication of this organ possesses the fullest justification. With the aim of placing on record the performances of all sections of the Club, I have obtained the willing co-operation of the sectional officials, who will produce their reports and views. This, of course, does not bar any member from submitting articles—in fact, they will be most welcome, for then it will be you writing your magazine, and I know articles by someone who was on the spot have a wide appeal amongst the Club fellows. My predecessor, A. A. Harley, will still contribute in the form of “General Honorary Secretary's Notes,” and it is hoped he will continue that popular feature “Ten Years Back.” This is greatly appreciated by our newer and younger members. In conclusion, I might add that any suggestion or criticism will be very gratefully received. With the co-operation of the Club officials, to whom I must again record my deepest appreciation, I have the greatest hope of attaining in some measure the high standard set up by my predecessors. A. A. Harley A. A. Harley previous Hon. Editor

items.label: December 1938
items.sum: Report of the Annual General Meeting of 27 September 1938: 46 present during the crisis, accounts adopted, J. R. McKay and T. Cotton made Life Members, W. L. Bayliss re-elected President and succeeded as Hon. Secretary by A. A. Harley, and the new captains named.
items.s: The Annual General Meeting. Report of the Annual General Meeting of 27 September 1938: 46 present during the crisis, accounts adopted, J. R. McKay and T. Cotton made Life Members, W. L. Bayliss re-elected President and succeeded as Hon. Secretary by A. A. Harley, and the new captains named. Belgrave Hall, 27th Sept., 1938. The President, W. L. Bayliss, presided, 46 members being present. the smallness in numbers being due to the crisis. The Hon. Secretary read the notice convening the meeting. The minutes of the last A.G.M. were read and confirmed. The Hon. Secretary then reported on the past year's activities. He commented on the good form of the cross-country teams, the improvement shown in Field Events and on the Track, and the exceptionally successful year enjoyed by the walkers. He hoped that the International situation, then menacing, would clear, and that the Club would again have a most successful year. This was accepted with acclamation. J. R. McKay (Hon. Auditor) read a written report of the accounts, the Hon. Treasurer having sent a letter regretting his absence. The reports were adopted on the proposal of F. G. Thomson, L. G. Bennett seconding. On behalf of the Committee, A. A. Harley proposed that .J R. McKay and T. Cotton be elected Life Members. He outlined the exceptionally good services that both these members had rendered the Club over a number of years. This proposal, when put by the President, was carried unanimously. The proposal by J. R. McKay that W. L. Bayliss should again be President was adopted with acclamation. W. L. Bayliss announced his retirement from the position of Gen. Hon. Secretary after eleven years, in which he had served the Club to the best of his ability, and seen the Club victorious in every Cross-Country and Road Walking Championship. He now thought that another member should carry on in this office, and announced that the Committee had considered the matter and that A. A. Harley was willing to allow his name to go forward on the assurance that he would receive the fullest co-operation. E. A. Duffett formally proposed and A. W. Penny seconded that A. A. Harley should be General Hon. Secretary, and the motion was adopted accordingly. The other officials were then elected as they appear in the new Handbook. The captaincies show a few changes. Bert Footer takes charge over the country again. He will be helped by Arthur Penny and Bert Lindsay. This is a new post for the latter. His steady running, knowledge of the courses and popularity should enable him to fill this post successfully. If versatility is the essence of a Track Captain, then we could have made no better choice than Frank Webb, whose experience and knowledge of our track runners should enable him to carry the Club on to further honours. He will have the co-operation of our new Field Event Captain, Charlie Jones, who is only a shade less than he is in versatility. From these deliberations I am sure that we will face the coming season with well justified optimism. W. L. Bayliss W. L. Bayliss President; presided; re-elected President; retired as Gen. Hon. items.s: The Three Miles Road Race. Report and full result of the club Three Miles Road Race handicap on 1 October 1938 over a new hilly course, won by Lionel Penny from N. C. Shrubb, with Arthur Penny fastest in 15 mins. 5 secs. 1st October, 1938. This year a different course was used. Instead of going out to the Windmill and home via that rough road across the Common and through the village, a lap of the hills was done. The actual times of the runners would suggest that the course is a little longer than the old one. Our old friend, George Still, started first, the last to start was Arthur Penny, who, although not on the scratch mark, gave proof of his fitness by clocking 15 mins. 5 secs. to record the fastest time. A. W. Jerman give us a good performance, being second fastest. The first to arrive was Lionel Penny, who was followed home by our promising junior, N. C. Shrubb. Then came our old friend, Bert Lindsey, to whom this race must have seemed like a sprint after his marathon efforts. Bert Smith was fourth. No doubt this will urge him on in his next handicap to gain those few seconds and so gain a place. Lionel's win was, no doubt, a great satisfaction to Arthur, whose years of experience, and his proven ability, enable him to give much useful brotherly advice. As regards the result as a whole, well, nobody can really expect fast times from everybody; some are fit, whilst others use this race as a loosener for the more serious work to come. RESULT. Pos. items.sum: Report on the two three-mile road novice races, open to Belgrave and unattached novices, which brought in new members.
items.s: Novice Races. Report on the two three-mile road novice races, open to Belgrave and unattached novices, which brought in new members. These races were open to both Belgrave and unattached novices and were both held on the road over three miles. They were instrumental in bringing us new members, which is, after all, the object of them. Many of the competitors gave useful performances, which they will soon be improving on if they are given the necessary encouragement and training. It is now up to them, for they have now only to report to their respective captains or vice-captains. We welcome them to the Club and wish them every success in their future races.

items.label: December 1938
items.sum: F. A. Walker's report of the season's first cross-country race, against Ealing H. from the Ballot Box, Perivale, won easily by Belgrave with A. R. Shaw first home; the printed result skips 14th place and its team scores do not match the club letters in the list.
items.s: Run v. Ealing H.—15th October. F. A. Walker's report of the season's first cross-country race, against Ealing H. from the Ballot Box, Perivale, won easily by Belgrave with A. R. Shaw first home; the printed result skips 14th place and its team scores do not match the club letters in the list. By F. A. Walker. Our first cross-country race of the season was against Ealing H. from their headquarters, the Ballot Box, Perivale. The team we sent was a strong one—good enough to win a "National"—if all were fit! The course was a fairly fast one. The Ealing fellows got away very fast at the start, having about a dozen men in the lead for the first three-quarters of a mile. After that they faded away one by one, then our lads had a "social" run amongst themselves. About two miles out we came across a miniature Everest which we had to climb, and what a climb! A. R. Shaw was the first man home, closely followed by six more Bels.; then two Ealing lads came in to split up the rest of our boys from the leaders. As we had the next five home we ran out easy winners. items.s: Match v. London University A.C. Report of the race over the club's 5 miles course at Wimbledon on 22 October against London University A.C., run with a club sealed handicap, led home by Arthur Penny, Bert Footer and Dan Patience. H. M. Quackenbos was second London man; A. T. Harper won the handicap; full club placings follow. The text names A. E. Smith third in the handicap where the table prints A. Smith. On Saturday, October 22nd, at Wimbledon, we entertained the members of the London University A.C. to a race over our 5 miles course. They were using this fixture as a trial for their runners, while we had our club sealed handicap in conjunction, so that a field of about 85 turned out. As most of our seniors were running they naturally soon went to the front, and eventually a small bunch of 3 runners drew away from the rest of the field. These were Arthur Penny, Bert Footer and Dan Patience. In the run home Arthur just beat Bert, with Dan third. We then had 10 more more "Bels" before the first London man, who was Alonzo, a member of the Blackheath Harriers. The second London man was none other than our own Junior Captain, H. M. Quackenbos. For the purpose of team scoring we deleted all our seniors, and this made W. E. Lucas—who was actually 7th in the race—first home, with G. Murdock and Tom Morrell next. We were easy winners on points, but trust our opponents enjoyed their run over our course. Our club handicap was won by A. T. Harper, who finished 20th in the actual race, and with 4-20 start he returned a net time of 27m. 27s. M. F. Edwards was second, his net time being 27m. 32s. Third place was taken by A. E. Smith. whose net time was 27m. 40s. We were pleased to see our prospective South of Thames Junior teams running well to the fore, and a newcomer in V. L. Green showed promising form. He comes to us from the Portsmouth A.C. and we hope he will enjoy his membership with the "Bels." Jimmy Kemp also displayed good form and we hope that he will retain it throughout the season, as so often Jimmy begins the season well and then fails to make our teams when the real "tests" come along. It was also good to see George Still "still going strong" (no pun), and even at his time of life he managed to beat a few of the young' uns. items.s: Match v. T.V.H. and Ashcombe-St. George's A.C. October 29th. A. S. Lindsey's report of the five-and-a-half-mile match at Cranford against T.V.H. and Ashcombe-St. George's A.C., where "A" men paced prospective South of the Thames juniors and Belgrave won by a big margin. Ashcombe took the first three places but were third; the result lists club letters and team scores as printed (Belgrave's nine places add to 102, not the printed 82; the results list jumps between 34 and 37 out of order). By A. S. Lindsey. The fact that over 30 of the Bels. travelled to Cranford for this fixture shows that it is still as popular as ever. There was an extra interest in the race, as a scheme by the Cross-country Captain, whereby an "A" team man took charge of two prospective "South of the Thames" juniors for the purpose of team packing and keeping an even pace throughout the race was tried out. From the finishing positions of many Juniors, it can be seen that the scheme had a good deal of success. Especially in the case of Rispin, who ran strongly all the way to finish in the first dozen. Owing to some "A" men not turning out, Footer had more than his share of men to take along. At one stage of the race he looked like a pocket size standard-bearer going into action, surrounded by a high wall of stalwarts. The five and a half miles course was a two lap one, mainly flat grassland with about three-quarters of a mile of woods. Ashcombe led the field home with the first three men, but were third in the team race, nine a side scoring. Although our "A" men were concentrating on getting their charges along they all packed well and we enjoyed a big margin win. Nutty Penny gained a medal given by the home club for being the first scoring man of the visiting teams. RESULTS. TEAM SCORES. Belgrave H. (4, 6, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 17) ... ... ... 82 pts.
